the-opportunity-list-stops-being-tenant-.why: A REAL CROSS-TENANT LEAK ON THE NEW BOOK-WIDE LIST. `Opportunity` drops out of the derived set, so `tenantScopeExtension` stops adding `organizationId` to its reads and `GET /opportunities` answers office A with office B's row. This is the plant the three isolation tests exist for — before decision 150 ruling 1 these records had NO cross-office assertion at all, because a `customerId`-only list cannot produce one. ⚠️ Expected to kill the opportunities isolation test AND the shared-name search, and to leave the RFQ and programme ones green: a plant that reddened all three would mean the tests were measuring the extension in general rather than their own route. ⛔ And this is LAYER ONE, not RLS — an HTTP assertion is answered by the application's filter, never by a database refusal; see `certificate-stored.e2e-spec.ts` for the measurement.

the-book-wide-list-forgets-who-owns-the-.why: THE SCOPING RULE REVERSED — a cross-OWNER leak inside one office, which is the half an isolation test cannot see. Every caller reaches the whole book, so a Sales/Relationship Officer lists opportunities on customers belonging to colleagues. It is the tempting edit precisely because it makes the screen fuller. Expected to kill `pins a caller without that code to the customers they own` by name and to LEAVE `lists the whole book for a caller who may reach any customer file` green — which is why both directions are asserted: the second test alone passes against this plant.

the-rfq-list-row-carries-its-raw-join.from:
const { opportunity, ...rfq } = row;
  return { ...rfqForWire(rfq), customer: opportunity.customer };
the-rfq-list-row-carries-its-raw-join.why: THE RAW-JOIN-AS-PAYLOAD SHAPE PUT BACK, in the exact form message 45 §2 measured: the `opportunity` join travels on the wire BESIDE the resolved `customer`, so one question has two answers and the web type describes neither. That is how the insurer column came to render as an empty cell — `undefined` prints as nothing in React and nobody is told. Expected to kill `lifts the customer onto the row and leaves the join behind` by name, and nothing else: the customer is still correct, which is what makes the defect quiet.

the-unopenable-customer-card-says-nothin.why: THE STATE THE OWNER'S SECOND WALK FOUND: the card is withheld as a control and says nothing about it, so it looks exactly like the clickable one and does nothing when pressed. ⚠️ This is the shape that reads as a BROKEN SCREEN rather than as a permission, which is why the sentence is the fix rather than removing the card. Expected to kill `a customer card the caller cannot open says why, and is not a control` by name, and nothing else — the card is still correctly not a control, which is what makes the defect quiet.

the-programmes-list-stops-naming-its-cus.why: THE BOOK-WIDE ROW WITHOUT ITS CUSTOMER — which is a row a reader who arrived from the sidebar cannot place at all, and the reason the ruling asks for the name in the first place. ⚠️ It is the EASY regression: the customer-scoped branch does not need the line (the reader already has the customer in hand), so deleting it looks like tidying. Expected to kill `lists everything the caller may read when no customer is in the URL` and `the book-wide list searches, and the term reaches the server`, both of which assert «Acme Trading» on the row.
